name: Diffuse Pediatric-Type High-Grade Glioma, H3-Wildtype, IDH-Wildtype

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Histological evidence of diffuse high-grade glioma with high cellularity, mitotic activity, and necrosis
Absence of H3 K27M and H3 G34 mutations confirmed by molecular testing
Absence of IDH1 and IDH2 mutations confirmed by molecular testing
MRI showing diffuse infiltrative lesion with contrast enhancement and mass effect

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of diffuse high-grade glioma with molecular confirmation of H3-wildtype and IDH-wildtype status
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histopathology and molecular genetic testing per WHO CNS tumor classification.

searchTerms: rapid onset of focal nerve problems
fast progression of localized brain deficits

pathognomonic.symptomName: Raised intracranial pressure symptoms (headache with vomiting)
searchTerms: headache with vomiting from high brain pressure
weakness on one side of body
loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision
problems with language or slurred speech
speech impairment or trouble finding words
sensory changes like pins and needles

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: CSF analysis typically non-specific; may show elevated protein
imaging: MRI showing diffuse infiltrative lesion with heterogeneous contrast enhancement
T2/FLAIR hyperintensity with mass effect and edema
genetic: Absence of H3 K27M and H3 G34 mutations
Absence of IDH1 and IDH2 mutations
Frequent TP53 mutations and other high-grade glioma-associated alterations
other: Histopathology showing high cellularity, mitoses, microvascular proliferation, and necrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of IDH1 or IDH2 mutation

redFlags: New onset seizures in a child
references: Louis DN, Perry A, Wesseling P, et al. The 2021 WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System: a summary. Neuro Oncol. 2021;23(8):1231-1251.
Orphanet: Diffuse Pediatric-Type High-Grade Glioma H3-Wildtype IDH-Wildtype (ORPHA:715724)
Jones DTW, Kieran MW, Bouffet E. Pediatric high-grade glioma: biologic insights and therapeutic opportunities. Neuro Oncol. 2017;19(8):1048-1059.
